name: Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum
charge: Not repenting after the mighty works done in them
summary: Most of Christ’s mighty works were done in Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum, and those cities did not repent. He upbraided them and measured them against Tyre, Sidon and Sodom, saying those cities would have repented at what these had seen, and that it would be more tolerable for them in the day of judgment. Capernaum, which had been exalted to heaven, was to be brought down to hell. Luke sets the same woes beside the sending of the seventy and the rule that to despise the messenger is to despise the one who sent him.
offenseFull: When John was cast into prison Christ departed into Galilee, left Nazareth, and came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim, and from that time he began to preach the same word John had preached, that men should repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand (Matthew 4:13-17). The study notes mark what the prophet calls that country: Galilee of the Gentiles (Isaiah 9:1-2). Zabulon and Nephthalim are tribes of the northern kingdom, and that is the key to who the gentiles are that the gospel goes to after the southern kingdom rejects it. These towns were not outsiders looking on. They were where the ministry lived.

Then he began to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not. Woe to Chorazin and woe to Bethsaida, for if the mighty works done in them had been done in Tyre and Sidon, those cities would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes. And Capernaum, which was exalted to heaven, would be brought down to hell, for if the mighty works done in her had been done in Sodom, it would have remained to that day (Matthew 11:20-24). The study notes put the charge in plain terms: men watched works no ordinary man could do and still would not turn, and other nations would have turned at what Israel watched and did not turn at. That is what a stiffnecked people looks like. Christ said the same thing another way, that if he had not come and spoken to them they had not had sin, but now they have no cloke for their sin (John 15:22-24).
judgmentFull: It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment than for Chorazin and Bethsaida, and more tolerable for the land of Sodom than for Capernaum (Matthew 11:20-24). The comparison takes away the comfort of measuring yourself against a city with a worse name; the greater the light given, the greater the reckoning for it. The class is careful about the timing: the judgment spoken of here is the one at the return of Christ, not a report that every part of the sentence had already fallen. And that is why the epistle asks how a man shall escape if he neglects so great salvation, spoken first by the Lord and confirmed by them that heard him (Hebrews 2:1-3).

Luke sets the same woes beside the sending out of the seventy, whom the Lord appointed and sent two and two before his face into every city and place where he himself would come (Luke 10:1-2). The class explains the pairing out of the law: no matter is established except at the mouth of two or three witnesses, so the men were sent in twos because they were being sent to bear witness, and to bear witness against a city is to bring judgment on it. Where they were received they said that the kingdom of God is come nigh; where they were not received they were to go out into the streets of that city and wipe off the very dust of it against them, and it would be more tolerable in that day for Sodom than for that city (Luke 10:8-12). The teaching class puts the working edge on that: the same word is carried into the cities now, and a man who walks past it cannot say afterward that he was never told.

What is done to the messenger is done to the one who sent him. He that hears them hears Christ, and he that despises them despises Christ, and he that despises Christ despises the one that sent him (Luke 10:13-16). That has been the standing answer of the nation to the men sent to gather it; the Lord said he had sent his servants the prophets, and they had been taken and slain and their bodies torn in pieces, and the house was left desolate (2 Esdras 1:32-33; Matthew 23:37-38). To be exalted to heaven and thrust down to hell is the prophet’s own language for Zion cast down from heaven to the earth in the day of his anger (Lamentations 2:1). And when the seventy came back with joy, Christ answered that he beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven (Luke 10:17-18): the going out of the witnesses was the beginning of the fall of the kingdom that held them.

text.text: And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim:
That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying,
The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles;
The people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.
From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.
The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.
Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not:
Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.

And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.
But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.
If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloke for their sin.
He that hateth me hateth my Father also.
If I had not done among them the works which none other man did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both me and my Father.
Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip.
For if the word spoken by angels was stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompence of reward;
How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;
After these things the Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself would come.
Therefore said he unto them, The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest.
And into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you, eat such things as are set before you:
And heal the sick that are therein, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.
But into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you not, go your ways out into the streets of the same, and say,
Even the very dust of your city, which cleaveth on us, we do wipe off against you: notwithstanding be ye sure of this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.
But I say unto you, that it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom, than for that city.

Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.
And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.
He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me; and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.
I sent unto you my servants the prophets, whom ye have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, saith the Lord.
Thus saith the Almighty Lord, Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind doth stubble.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger!
And the seventy returned again with joy, saying, Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through thy name.
And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.
